note: Canonical parity prompts for the Qwen 3.6 checkpoints. `tokens` was produced by the oracle's own `llama-tokenize --ids --no-bos` against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q4_K_M.gguf. The Qwen vocabulary has NO BOS — nothing is prepended, and a harness that prepends one is wrong. Both checkpoints share the tokenizer, so the same ids drive the 27B. At parity time scripts/ref-dump.sh re-derives the authoritative ids from the eval-callback token echo; the ids here drive logits-dump directly.

prompts.note: Short code prompt. One prefill chunk; the DeltaNet layers see a short recurrence, so a divergence here is arithmetic, not state carry.

prompts.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. In 2024, the team reported a 3.7x speedup on the Q4_K_M kernels, down from 128 ms to just 34 ms per token. Costs fell from $0.012 to $0.004 -- roughly a third. Not bad for a Tuesday afternoon of profiling!
prompts.note: Mixed prose, digits, currency and punctuation. Exercises the tokenizer's number/symbol handling and the router on non-code text.

prompts.text:
Gated DeltaNet replaces softmax attention on three layers out of every four. Where an attention layer keeps every past key and value and re-reads them at each step, a DeltaNet layer keeps one fixed-size matrix per head and rewrites it as tokens arrive. The state does not grow with the sequence, so the cost of a forward pass is linear in the number of tokens rather than quadratic, and the memory a long conversation occupies stops depending on how long the conversation is. What the layer gives up in exchange is direct access to any particular earlier token: everything it remembers has to have been written into that matrix at the time, and anything overwritten is gone.

The write rule is what makes the layer more than a running average. For each token the layer computes a query, a key and a value, normalizes the query and the key to unit length, and then, instead of simply adding the outer product of key and value to the state, it first reads what the state currently predicts for that key and subtracts it. The difference between the value that arrived and the value the state already held is scaled by a per-head gate between zero and one and only that difference is written back. A gate near zero leaves the state untouched, a gate near one replaces the old association outright, and everything between interpolates. A second gate decays the whole state multiplicatively before the write, so associations that are never refreshed fade instead of accumulating forever.

Because the state is carried forward token by token, the recurrence is sequential by nature, which is awkward for a prefill that wants to process hundreds of tokens at once. The usual remedy is to process the sequence in fixed chunks, computing within a chunk the same result the step-by-step recurrence would have produced, using a triangular solve to untangle the mutual dependence of the writes inside the chunk, and only then folding the chunk's aggregate effect into the running state. The chunked form and the recurrent form are algebraically identical, but they accumulate their floating-point sums in different orders, so on real hardware they agree to a tolerance rather than exactly, and any harness that compares the two has to say which tolerance it means.

Interleaving the two layer types is what keeps the model from having to choose. The full-attention layers, one in four, can look at any earlier position directly and cheaply repair whatever the linear layers have blurred; the linear layers carry information forward at constant cost between them. A depthwise convolution over the fused query, key and value stream sits in front of each DeltaNet layer and gives it a short exact window over the last few tokens, which the recurrence alone would smear. The convolution keeps its own small state, three columns wide, and that state has to be checkpointed and rolled back alongside the recurrent matrices whenever a speculative decode walks a branch it later abandons. Getting either one wrong produces output that looks fluent for a dozen tokens and then quietly drifts, which is exactly the failure mode a parity harness exists to catch before anyone ships it.
prompts.note: Long prose (multi-hundred tokens): the DeltaNet state is carried over a long recurrence and the full-attention layers see a long KV span, so state-carry bugs that a short prompt hides show up here.
